deportes.t: We have not found any strength training trial in hikers. Going downhill puts a lot of load on the knee, and in the Alps three out of four falls happened on the way down: strong legs for braking could help, but it is a deduction.
p: In 12 healthy people, walking downhill loaded the knee with 8 times body weight, compared with 3.9 on the flat; 80% of it came from the muscles (Kuster 1997).
A 2020 review: poles reduce the load on the legs but increase cardiovascular effort; with a heavy rucksack they can also help with balance.
The authors of the Alps study recommend regular physical activity with eccentric work (that of a muscle braking), but it is their opinion, not a finding.
encajar: Rest enough before starting the descent and take breaks on the way down: the authors of the Alps study recommend this.
Without trials of its own, the strength guidance is the general one, that of «Another sport».

lesiones.t: In hikers in the Austrian Alps (Alpine police data), about 75% of falls happened on the way down and almost 60% were due to slipping.

isla.t: Walking up to La Rambleta, on the Teide, requires a booking on Tenerife ON, and the trails may close because of ice, snow, wind or frost even if you have one.
On the Teide, altitude sickness usually brings a headache after 2–12 hours; with confusion, drowsiness, unsteady walking or breathlessness at rest, call 112 and go down with someone.
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month. Protect yourself even if it feels cool.
In the heat, avoid walking in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
On the day of the hike, check Tenerife ON for alerts or closed trails; tell someone your route and do not go alone.

no: That strength training prevents falls or injuries in the mountains: we have not found any trial that tests this in hikers.
That poles always pay off: when walking without a load, the 2020 review advises weighing up the pros and cons.

deportes.t: The evidence points to maximal strength training out of the water being what most improves swimming performance, although 7 of 16 studies found no effect at all.
p: A review of 16 studies (Amaro et al. 2019): dry-land maximal strength training was the most effective method for performance; 7 studies found neither improvement nor worsening.
The same review puts forward plyometrics (jumps) as the most effective method for starts and turns.
deportes.dosis: The review mentions 6 to 12 weeks, with 2–4 sessions a week (about 24 in total), and its authors suggest 2–3 sets of 3–5 repetitions at 80–90% of the maximum you can lift once.
encajar: The review mentions programmes of 6 to 12 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to swim better because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).
We have no data on combining strength training and swimming on the same day; in running and cycling, with 3 hours or more between the two there was no significant loss of explosive strength.

isla.t: Swim at beaches with lifeguards and always check the flag before going in. When the waves are unusually big, stay away from the sea; when there is a swell, do not do sport in the water.
If a current carries you away, do not swim against it: float so as not to tire yourself, wave your arm and shout for help, or swim out of it parallel to the shore.
According to the association Canarias, 1500 Km de Costa, of the 69 people who drowned in the Canary Islands in 2025, 74% were men and 46% had gone into the sea during a pre-alert or alert.
Swim parallel to the shore, with someone else and never at night; get out if you feel tired or cold, and do not drink alcohol if you are going to swim.
For sport in the heat, the WHO asks for sunscreen of factor 30 or more, a hat and sunglasses; the Government of the Canary Islands advises factor 50+, also on cloudy days.

no: That strength training makes you swim faster: almost half of the studies reviewed found no effect.
That jumps improve all your swimming: the review only puts them forward for starts and turns.

deportes.t: The evidence points to strength training with heavy loads slightly improving running economy, that is, using less energy at the same pace. Combining methods might help a little more, with low certainty.
p: A meta-analysis of 31 studies with 652 middle- and long-distance runners (Llanos-Lagos et al. 2024): heavy loads improved economy with a small effect and moderate certainty.
Combining methods, such as medium loads and jumps, had a moderate effect, but with low certainty; medium loads alone and isometrics (without movement) showed no effect.
Jumps (plyometrics) only improved economy at 12 km/h or less, that is, at 5:00 min/km or slower; in the main analysis they had no effect.
Heavy loads might pay off more in runners with a high VO2max (a lot of aerobic capacity) and at high speeds.
deportes.dosis: Heavy loads, of at least 80% of the maximum weight you can lift once, 2–4 days a week for 6–14 weeks; for example, half squats, leg presses and deadlifts.
encajar: In 43 studies, combining strength training with running or cycling did not reduce maximal strength or muscle; explosive strength did suffer, especially in the same session (Schumann 2022).
If you do both on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between running and strength training: with that gap there was no significant loss of explosive strength.
The programmes lasted 6 to 24 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to run better because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid running in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
Acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks of sessions in the heat (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, run for less time, more gently and in the cooler hours.
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month. Protect yourself even if it feels cool.
A one-day trip up the Teide does not acclimatise you to altitude: partial acclimatisation takes 5 to 7 days, according to the IOC consensus for athletes.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That it lowers your times: the meta-analysis measured running economy, which is not the same as your finishing time.
That any strength training will do: medium loads and isometrics did not improve running economy.
That there are as many data on women: only 180 of the 652 runners studied were women.

deportes.t: With low certainty, studies suggest that heavy leg strength training might improve pedalling efficiency, maximal power and performance, without changing maximal aerobic capacity (VO2max).
p: A meta-analysis of 17 studies with 262 cyclists (Llanos-Lagos et al. 2026): heavy strength training improved efficiency, peak power and performance; VO2max did not change.
Only two studies recruited women only; in total, 60 of the 262 participants were women.
deportes.dosis: Improvements likely from about 8 weeks or with 2 sessions a week, with heavy loads and 3–4 sets per exercise, in 4 leg exercises.
encajar: In season, 1 weekly session maintained the gains for 13 weeks in a study with cyclists; for health, the WHO asks adults for at least 2 days.
If you do strength training and cycling on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between them: with 20 minutes or less, explosive strength suffered (Schumann 2022).
Improvements seem likely from about 8 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to pedal better because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid cycling in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
Acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks of sessions in the heat (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier rides in the cooler hours.
Climbing the Teide, the sun is stronger: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That strength training increases your aerobic capacity: VO2max did not change in these studies.
That the result is certain: the authors themselves rate the evidence as low certainty.

deportes.t: There are few studies: in one, maximal strength training with pull-ups and dips made surfers paddle faster, but no study has shown that it improves surfing on the wave.
p: A trial with competitive and recreational surfers (Coyne 2017): after training pull-ups and dips, they paddled faster in sprints of 5 to 15 m and over 400 m.
The improvement seemed to depend on starting strength and was greater in the weaker surfers (Coyne’s thesis, 2015).
A review of 8 studies (Donaldson 2022): maximal upper-body strength improved paddling, and training on unstable surfaces did not help.
deportes.dosis: Maximal-strength pull-ups and dips, 3 times a week for 5 weeks; the abstract and the thesis do not give the loads.
encajar: The trial lasted 5 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to paddle faster because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).
In SUP, paddling more than 4.8 hours a week was a risk factor for injury, as were competing or being over 46 (Furness 2017).

lesiones.t: In 240 stand-up paddleboarders, more than half of them competitive, there were 3.63 injuries per 1,000 hours of practice (Furness 2017); we have no verified data for surfing.

isla.t: In the Canary Islands, beaches in the north are usually more dangerous than those in the south, because of the wind, the waves and the currents.
Before you go out, check the forecast: wind and sea can change suddenly on the coast. Do not go out at dusk or when there is a swell, and never alone.
If a current carries you away, do not paddle against it: stay with the board, which keeps you afloat (RNLI), call for help by waving your arm and get out parallel to the shore.
Use sun protection of factor 50+ and keep using it on cloudy days too, as the Government of the Canary Islands asks.

no: That strength training improves your surfing on the wave: no study in the review showed it.
That training on unstable surfaces will help you: in the review, it did not work.
That it applies equally to SUP: the trial was done with surfers, and for SUP we only have injury data.

deportes.t: We know of no strength studies in diving, but the Divers Alert Network (DAN) calls for sufficient strength, cardiovascular health and, above all, aerobic capacity for what the environment demands.
p: According to DAN, recreational diving can demand a moderate to high aerobic level, and freediving is considered vigorous exercise.
DAN considers regular physical activity, both aerobic and strength, essential, such as swimming lengths, strength training and flexibility and balance exercises.
encajar: At least 6 weeks before a diving trip, gradually increase your physical activity, as DAN advises.
If you are over 40 and do not exercise regularly, DAN advises seeing a doctor before you start training.
Do not dive if you are ill (DAN).

isla.t: Before flying, DAN asks for at least 12 hours after a no-decompression dive, 18 after several dives in a day or over several days, and substantially longer if you made decompression stops.
After diving, going up the Teide by car or cable car (up to 3,555 m) carries the same risk as flying and calls for the same waiting times, according to DAN Europe, from about 700 m of ascent.
Do not dive alone and mark where you are with a buoy, as the Government of the Canary Islands asks.
Before you go out, check the forecast: wind and sea can change suddenly on the coast. Do not go out at dusk.

no: That strength training makes you a better diver: we know of no studies that measure it; DAN includes it in general fitness.
That the waiting times before flying completely prevent decompression sickness: DAN says they do not guarantee it, and waiting longer reduces the risk.
That the waiting times apply if you have symptoms: DAN gives them for divers without symptoms; if you have any, get medical care.

deportes.t: A meta-analysis of 20 studies links greater jump power and greater upper-body explosive strength with greater clubhead speed; it is an association: training them might help, but we have no trials that prove it.
p: Brennan 2024: clubhead speed was associated with jump impulse (correlation zr 0.82), upper-body explosive strength (0.67) and jump power (0.66).
By contrast, flexibility and balance were not associated with clubhead speed (−0.04 and −0.06).
encajar: Without verified golf trials, the basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid playing in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
For sport in the heat, the WHO asks for sunscreen of factor 30 or more, a hat, sunglasses and loose, light-coloured clothing; the Government of the Canary Islands advises factor 50+.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That stretching or balance training gives you more clubhead speed: they were not associated with it.
More clubhead speed from strength training: what we have are associations, not trials.

deportes.t: We know of no strength studies in padel. In tennis, strength training and combined programmes increased serve speed, and isolated abs and lower back work did not (Deng 2025); in padel this can only be extrapolated to smashes (a deduction).
p: A meta-analysis of 16 studies with tennis players (Deng et al. 2025): strength training had a small effect on serve speed and combined programmes a moderate one.
In the combined programmes there was publication bias (studies with no effect may be missing): the authors call for more high-quality studies.
The meta-analysis only measured serve speed, in tennis players aged about 11 to 42, and does not mention padel.
deportes.dosis: In tennis players, strength training 2–3 times a week for 4–36 weeks; combined programmes, 3 times a week for 6–8 weeks (8–36 sessions).
encajar: The tennis programmes lasted 4 to 36 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect changes in your shots: treat it as maintenance (deduction).
The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).

lesiones.t: In 8 studies, most of them in Spain, with 2,022 players: 3 injuries per 1,000 hours of training and 8 per 1,000 matches, mainly of tendons and muscles (Dahmen 2023).
zonas: Elbow: the most frequent, especially tennis elbow

isla.t: In the heat, avoid playing in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier matches.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That isolated abs and lower back work improves your shots: in tennis it did not increase serve speed.
That what applies to tennis applies to your serve: in padel the ball is struck at waist height or below.
Exact injury figures: the studies were of low to moderate quality and the literature is limited.

deportes.t: The gym is strength training, and the evidence is solid: according to the ACSM (2026, 137 systematic reviews), compared with not training it improves strength, muscle, power and physical function. What matters most is working all the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week and keeping it up.
p: The ACSM (2026) brought together 137 systematic reviews with more than 30,000 healthy adults: compared with not training, strength training improved strength, muscle size, power, walking speed and balance.
ACSM 2026, in healthy adults: training to muscular failure, choosing machines or free weights and complex periodisation (systematic variation) did not change results consistently.
For muscle, loads from 30% to 100% of the maximum you can lift once worked; for maximal strength, heavier loads of 80% or more did better.
deportes.dosis: For strength, the ACSM 2026 proposes loads of 80% of the maximum you can lift once and 2–3 sets per exercise; to build muscle, about 10 sets per muscle group per week; and for power, moderate loads (30–70%) moved as fast as possible on the way up.
encajar: Train all the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week and build up gradually: it matters more than looking for a «perfect» plan (ACSM 2026, in adults).
Choose a plan you can keep up: according to the ACSM, the best plan is the one you stick with, and one too demanding to maintain loses its effectiveness.
If you combine strength training with running or cycling on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between them: with 20 minutes or less, explosive strength suffered (Schumann 2022).

lesiones.t: According to the ACSM, strength training is safe for healthy adults of all ages. In 28 studies, traditional strength training caused the fewest injuries and strongman the most (Serafim 2023). Among the weight-training sports, bodybuilding had the lowest rate, 0.24 to 1 injury per 1,000 hours, and the most common injuries were strains, tendinitis and sprains (Keogh 2017).
zonas: Shoulder: the most injured area in bodybuilding and powerlifting

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That training to failure or a complex plan gives more results: the ACSM saw no consistent differences in healthy adults.
That more sets always give more: beyond about 18–20 per muscle group per week, muscle gains less and less (ACSM 2026).
That these guidelines are enough if you compete: according to the ACSM, athletes and people who train hard need plans specific to their sport and goals.

deportes.t: Calisthenics is strength training with your own body weight, and it works: according to the ACSM (2026), body weight, resistance bands and training at home bring clear gains in strength, muscle and physical function. In small trials, press-ups gave as much strength as the bench press with a similar load.
p: With the load matched, press-ups gave strength gains similar to the bench press: in 30 university students with weight-training experience, using resistance bands over 5 weeks (Calatayud 2015), and in 18 young men over 8 weeks, who also gained as much muscle as the bench press group (Kikuchi 2017).

Over 4 weeks, progressively harder press-ups improved the maximal bench press of 23 moderately trained men, just as bench press training did; muscle thickness did not change in either group (Kotarsky 2018).
In 28 untrained men, 8 weeks of calisthenics raised the press-up test by 16.4% and the pull-up test by 39.2%, improved posture and lowered fat mass; the control group did not change (Thomas 2017).

For muscle, loads from 30% of the maximum worked; for maximal strength, 80% or more (ACSM 2026). With body weight, that calls for hard variations, bands or added weight, as in the Calatayud trial (deduction).
deportes.dosis: In the press-up trials, 2 to 3 sessions a week for 4 to 8 weeks; with bands, 5 sets of 6 repetitions, with a band that only allowed 6 (Calatayud 2015).
encajar: Work your legs and trunk too: the ACSM asks for all the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week.
When a variation feels easy, move on to a harder one: that is how the effort was kept up in the press-up trial (Kotarsky 2018).
You don’t need to train to failure, but every set should be hard: that is what the ACSM (2026) asks for.

lesiones.t: In 184 calisthenics practitioners there were 1.3 injuries per 1,000 hours of training, more than 70% from the shoulder to the hand and mostly to muscle or tendon (Kaiser 2018). Of 93 street workout practitioners, 62.4% had been injured in the past year; tendinopathy was the most frequent diagnosis, and previous injuries and more vigorous activity were associated with more injuries (Ngo 2021).
zonas: Shoulder: 23.0% of injuries in street workout

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
For sport in the heat, the WHO asks for sunscreen of factor 30 or more, a hat and sunglasses; the Government of the Canary Islands advises factor 50+, also on cloudy days.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier sessions.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That any set of press-ups is as good as the bench press: in the trials the load was comparable, using bands or adjusting the position.
That the trials apply to the whole body: they mainly measured press-ups and the bench press, with few participants.
That calisthenics causes fewer injuries than the gym: we have not found studies that compare them directly.

deportes.t: In combat sports, strength training improved strength and power and, in boxing, punching power and speed, although the studies were of low quality (Cid-Calfucura 2023). In elite amateur boxing, those who punch hardest have more maximal and explosive strength in their legs (Beattie and Ruddock 2022).
p: A review of 20 studies (5 in boxing) with 504 Olympic combat sport athletes: strength training improved maximal strength, power, flexibility and balance and, in boxing, punching power and speed (Cid-Calfucura 2023).
In 15 boxers from the Brazilian national team (9 men and 6 women), strength and power were closely related to punch impact, with correlations of 0.67 to 0.85 (Loturco 2016).

According to a review, in elite amateur boxing punch impact is associated with maximal leg strength and with explosive strength in the legs and arms; maximal arm strength is not (Beattie and Ruddock 2022).
deportes.dosis: With combat sport athletes, 2 to 6 sessions a week for 4 to 20 weeks; half of the programmes lasted 4 to 8 weeks (Cid-Calfucura 2023).
encajar: The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).

For your legs, work on maximal and explosive strength; for your arms, explosive strength only: that is what the review advises for punching harder, although trials confirming it are still lacking (Beattie and Ruddock 2022).
The programmes lasted 4 to 20 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday don’t expect changes in your punch: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

lesiones.t: In 66 boxers in the British team (2005–2009), the hand was the most injured area, in training and in competition, and concussions were comparatively few (Loosemore 2015). In 152 Muay Thai practitioners, the legs were the most injured and, in amateurs and professionals, the head came next (Gartland 2001).
zonas: Hand: the most injured in the British team; the study calls for protecting hands and wrists
Head, neck and face: 52.5% of injuries in professional kickboxing
Legs: the most injured in Muay Thai, and 39.8% in professional kickboxing

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier sessions.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That maximal arm strength is the key to punching: in elite boxing it was not associated with punch impact (Beattie and Ruddock 2022).

That repeated blows to the head leave no trace: in 224 professional boxers and MMA fighters, more fights and more years of fighting were associated with lower brain volume and slower processing speed (Bernick 2015).
Firm evidence: trials in boxing are lacking, even more so with women; in the review, 428 of the 504 athletes were men (Beattie and Ruddock 2022; Cid-Calfucura 2023).

deportes.t: In a trial with 14 competitive Brazilian jiu-jitsu athletes, adding maximal strength training 3 times a week raised the squat by 15% and the bench press by 11%; those who only did jiu-jitsu did not improve (Øvretveit and Tøien 2018). In judo, strength training improved throws (Cid-Calfucura 2023).
p: In that trial, those who added strength training also jumped 9% higher and did more repetitions: 33% more pull-ups, 32% more press-ups and 13% more sit-ups (Øvretveit and Tøien 2018).

A review of 20 studies of Olympic combat sports (7 in judo and 2 in wrestling) found that strength training improved maximal strength, power, flexibility and balance and, in judo, throwing techniques (Cid-Calfucura 2023).
deportes.dosis: With competitive jiu-jitsu athletes, 3 sessions a week: 4 sets of 4 repetitions at 85% or more of the maximum in the squat and bench press, and 4 sets of pull-ups to failure (Øvretveit and Tøien 2018).
encajar: The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).
Add strength training to your sport without cutting sessions: in the trial, both groups carried on with their usual jiu-jitsu (Øvretveit and Tøien 2018).
After every session on the mat, shower with antimicrobial soap, wash your kit every day and don’t share towels or equipment: that is what the NATA asks to prevent skin infections (Zinder 2010).
In 1–2 weeks of holiday, treat it as maintenance: in the review, the programmes lasted 4 to 20 weeks (deduction).

lesiones.t: In Brazilian jiu-jitsu competition there were 9.2 injuries per 1,000 match exposures; 78% were orthopaedic, and the most frequent was to the elbow, from the arm bar (Scoggin 2014). At the 2008 and 2012 Olympic Games, on average about 11–12% of judokas were injured, and the most common cause was being thrown (Pocecco 2013).
zonas: Elbow: the most frequent injury in jiu-jitsu competition, from the arm bar
Knee, shoulder and fingers: the sprains, strains and bruises most reported in judo
Skin: contagious infections in mat sports, from viruses, fungi or bacteria

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier sessions.

Canarian wrestling (lucha canaria), an Asset of Cultural Interest since 2018, is the islands’ own form of wrestling: it is fought standing in a circular ring, and you win by making your opponent touch the ground with anything other than the soles of the feet; there is no ground fighting, and no joint locks or chokes (Decree 82/2018).
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That your sport alone is enough to gain strength if you already compete: in the trial, those who only did jiu-jitsu did not improve in any test (Øvretveit and Tøien 2018).
That the trial applies to everyone: it involved only 14 men who already competed, and it measured short-term effects.
Firm evidence: in the review, the quality of the studies was low, and 428 of the 504 athletes were men (Cid-Calfucura 2023).

deportes.t: According to a review, in karate strength training improved kata scores, although the studies were few and of low quality, and it found none in taekwondo that met its criteria (Cid-Calfucura 2023). In older adults, Olympic combat sports improved the chair stand test (Valdés-Badilla 2021).
p: A review of 20 studies (5 in karate) with 504 Olympic combat sport athletes: strength training improved maximal strength, power, flexibility and balance and, in karate, scores in the Gankaku kata (Cid-Calfucura 2023).

In older adults, 12 trials with 735 participants averaging 69.6 years: Olympic combat sports (boxing, judo, karate and taekwondo) improved the chair stand test, and more than 80% stuck with the programmes (Valdés-Badilla 2021).
deportes.dosis: With combat sport athletes, 2 to 6 sessions a week for 4 to 20 weeks; half of the programmes lasted 4 to 8 weeks (Cid-Calfucura 2023).
encajar: The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).
If you combine strength training with running or cycling on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between them: with 20 minutes or less, explosive strength suffered (Schumann 2022).
The programmes lasted 4 to 20 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday don’t expect changes: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

lesiones.t: In competition karate (28 studies) there was on average 1 injury every 11 bouts, about 25 minutes of fighting, and the vast majority were minor, mostly bruises (Lystad 2020). In competition taekwondo, the turning kick caused 56.9% of injuries in men and 49.8% in women, and poor blocking skills were one of the main causes (Pieter 2012).
zonas: Head and neck: the most injured in karate, with a median of 57.9% of injuries
Legs: 44.5% of injuries in competition taekwondo in men and 53.1% in women
Head and neck in taekwondo: 29.6% of injuries in men and 15.2% in women

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier sessions.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That jumps on their own will improve your karate or taekwondo: in a meta-analysis of combat sport athletes, mostly under 18, jumping and leg strength improved, but performance specific to each sport did not clearly improve (Ojeda-Aravena 2023).
That karate or taekwondo prevent falls in older people: in 8 studies with 322 older adults, there were no differences in fall risk or in falls (Valdés-Badilla 2022).
Firm evidence: in the review, the quality of the studies was low, and 428 of the 504 athletes were men (Cid-Calfucura 2023).

deportes.t: In climbers, climbing plus strength training improved climbing-specific tests, such as hanging from the fingers, more than climbing alone; and training the finger flexors improved finger strength and forearm endurance. The studies are few and short, and most of their climbers were men (Stien 2022).
p: A review of 11 studies with 225 climbers: in its meta-analysis (5 studies, 110 climbers), strength training improved climbing-specific tests, such as hanging from the fingers or finger strength, more than climbing alone (Stien 2022).
Compared with climbing alone, training the finger flexors improved finger strength, the speed of applying it and, above all, forearm endurance (Stien 2022).
deportes.dosis: In the studies, 2 to 4 sessions a week (most often 3) for 4 to 10 weeks; the exercise used most was hanging from the fingers on a fingerboard (Stien 2022).
encajar: The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).
Add strength to your climbing, without climbing less: the studies compared climbing plus strength training with climbing alone (Stien 2022).
According to a review, an injury-prevention strength programme reduced shoulder and elbow injuries in climbers (Quarmby 2023).
Increase your climbing hours and loads gradually, and watch for signs of overuse: that is what the authors of the Swedish study ask (Backe 2009).
The programmes lasted 4 to 10 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday don’t expect changes: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

lesiones.t: In a sample from the Swedish Climbing Association there were 4.2 injuries per 1,000 hours of climbing, 93% from overuse, and the most common were inflammation of the fingers and wrists (Backe 2009). According to a review of 34 studies, climbing at higher intensity, bouldering, lower grip strength, the crimp grip and a previous injury were associated with more overuse injuries (Quarmby 2023).
zonas: Fingers and wrists: the most common injuries, almost all from overuse
Shoulders: with the fingers, where most overuse injuries occur in adults

isla.t: In Teide National Park, climbing must be notified in advance through the park’s electronic application, with bookings and quotas, and is only allowed in designated areas, such as the Roques de García or La Catedral. Carving holds is forbidden, chalk must match the colour of the rock, and climbing may be banned in certain places and periods to protect birds (Decree 182/2025).
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month.
In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That it will raise your climbing grade: the review says it may improve, but its studies could not be pooled and the results were mixed (Stien 2022).
That arm work in the gym is enough: in one of the studies, it did not significantly improve the climbers’ grade (Stien 2022).
Firm evidence: there are few studies, none longer than 10 weeks, and none with women only (Stien 2022).

deportes.t: In people over 60, yoga improved leg strength and flexibility, also compared with other activities, and balance compared with doing nothing (Sivaramakrishnan 2019). In older adults, Pilates improved strength, with moderate certainty, and balance and flexibility, with low certainty (Fernández-Rodríguez 2021).
p: In 17 trials with 967 people over 60 without a specific disease, yoga improved leg strength (getting up from a chair) and lower-body flexibility, compared with doing nothing and with other activities, such as walking (Sivaramakrishnan 2019).

A review of 39 studies with people over 60: compared with no exercise or their usual life, Pilates improved strength and reduced the risk of falls (moderate certainty), and improved balance, flexibility and functional capacity (low certainty) (Fernández-Rodríguez 2021).
deportes.dosis: In the yoga trials with older adults, 2 sessions a week were most common (otherwise 3), of 60 minutes, for 4 to 28 weeks (Sivaramakrishnan 2019).
encajar: The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).

According to the 2024 Compendium, yoga in general (2.3 MET) and Pilates (2.8 MET) are light activities, below 3 MET: for the moderate aerobic activity the WHO asks for, add walking, swimming or cycling (deduction).
In 1–2 weeks of holiday, treat it as maintenance: the programmes in the trials lasted 4 to 28 weeks (deduction).

lesiones.t: In 94 trials with 8,430 participants, yoga caused no more adverse events than usual care or other exercise (Cramer 2015). In US emergency departments in 2014, there were 57.9 yoga injuries per 100,000 practitioners aged 65 or over, compared with 11.9 among those aged 18 to 44 (Swain and McGwin 2016).
zonas: Trunk: 46.6% of yoga injuries treated in US emergency departments (2001–2014)

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
For sport in the heat, the WHO asks for sunscreen of factor 30 or more, a hat and sunglasses; the Government of the Canary Islands advises factor 50+, also on cloudy days.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That it replaces strength training: in the trials, strength was only measured by getting up from a chair, and none used a dynamometer (Sivaramakrishnan 2019).
That it improves balance more than other activities: compared with them, the difference was not significant (Sivaramakrishnan 2019).
That it applies equally to young people: the studies in these two reviews are with people over 60.

deportes.t: Compared with no exercise, high-intensity functional training, such as CrossFit, improved strength and endurance; for endurance it was neither better nor worse than classic endurance training, and it has not yet been compared with strength training (Wilke and Mohr 2020).
p: In 16 studies with 864 people, with mean ages from 11.7 to 72.8, high-intensity functional training improved strength and endurance compared with no exercise, but not balance (Wilke and Mohr 2020).
Compared with classic endurance training, continuous or interval-based, it improved endurance just as much, no more and no less (Wilke and Mohr 2020).
deportes.dosis: In almost all the studies, 2 to 4 sessions a week, from a few minutes to 40 each, for 4 to 18 weeks (Wilke and Mohr 2020).
encajar: The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).
Train with a coach who supervises you: in the studies, lack of supervision was associated with more injuries, although their quality does not allow firm conclusions (Rodríguez 2022).
The programmes lasted 4 to 18 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday don’t expect changes: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

lesiones.t: In CrossFit, studies report between 0.2 and 18.9 injuries per 1,000 hours of training, a rate similar to that of weightlifting and powerlifting. Among other factors, a previous injury and training without a coach’s supervision were associated with more injuries (Rodríguez 2022).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier sessions.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That it is well studied: in a review of 31 articles on CrossFit, only 2 studies had a high level of evidence and a low risk of bias, and its meta-analysis found no significant effect (Claudino 2018).
That it improves balance: compared with no exercise, it did not (Wilke and Mohr 2020).
That you will gain more strength than with weights: there are no studies comparing them (Wilke and Mohr 2020).

deportes.t: For a sport without its own guide, the basis is the general one: the WHO recommends that adults do strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups; from 5 to 17 years, at least 3.
p: WHO 2020: adults, 150–300 minutes a week of moderate activity or 75–150 of vigorous activity; from 5 to 17 years, an average of 60 minutes a day, moderate to vigorous.
According to the WHO, for all ages some physical activity is better than none.
From the age of 65, the WHO adds varied activity that emphasises balance and strength, on 3 or more days a week.
ACSM 2026, in healthy adults: training to muscular failure, choosing machines or free weights and complex periodisation (systematic variation) did not change results consistently.
deportes.dosis: For strength, the ACSM 2026 proposes loads of 80% of the maximum you can lift once and 2–3 sets per exercise; to build muscle, about 10 sets per muscle group per week.
encajar: Train all the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week and build up gradually: it matters more than looking for a «perfect» plan (ACSM 2026, in adults).
If you combine strength training with running or cycling on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between them: with 20 minutes or less, explosive strength suffered (Schumann 2022).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.
If your sport is in the sea, swim at beaches with lifeguards and always check the flag before going in.

no: That general strength training improves your particular sport: without studies of that sport, we cannot say so.
That training to failure or a complex plan gives more results: the ACSM saw no consistent differences in healthy adults.
